analysis.file_name: G10 Inflation Monitor_ Core Inflation Accelerates Outside Canada(1).pdf
analysis.title: G10 Inflation Monitor: Core Inflation Accelerates Outside Canada; Trimmed Measures Look More Benign
key_insights: Exclusion-based core inflation rose year over year in September in Japan (2.4% vs 1.9% in August), the UK (2.8% vs 2.6%), the US (3.1% vs 3.0%) and the Euro area (2.5% vs 2.4%), and was unchanged in Canada at 2.1%.

On a month-over-month annualized basis, exclusion-based core accelerated in Japan (6.0% vs 2.4%), the Euro area (3.6% vs 1.3%), the UK (4.0% vs 2.8%) and the US (3.9% vs 3.2%), and slowed in Canada (1.5% vs 3.1%).

US trimmed inflation runs well below exclusion core (Dallas Fed trimmed mean +2.3% yoy, GS trimmed core 2.1% yoy). GS US economists say trimmed mean remains a useful signal of underlying inflation because much of what is trimmed reflects one-off effects of tariffs, the energy shock, and AI-related price pressures and mismeasurement.
GS trimmed core slowed on a month-over-month annualized basis in Canada (1.3% vs 2.8%), the Euro area (1.8% vs 2.6%), Japan (2.2% vs 2.4%) and the UK (2.8% vs 3.4%).

GS harmonized core is generally close to central banks' preferred measures on a 3-month basis in most developed markets, but is notably higher in Japan, where owned housing, which GS excludes from the harmonized measure, weighs on the central bank's core measure.

September US core CPI surprised to the upside, driven partly by firmer owners' equivalent rent (+0.7% yoy as cited) and a large rise in toys and games (+4.2% yoy). Canada's BoC-preferred core measures surprised to the downside, partly on car rental (-3.9% mom) and travel services (-2.4% mom) declines. Elsewhere core was broadly in line.

Over the last 12 months, monthly headline and core prints have surprised to the downside outside the Euro area, with the largest cumulative core surprises in Canada (-80bp), Japan (-50bp) and the UK (-23bp).

On a 3-month annualized basis, core goods inflation accelerated in the US (PCE, 1.7% vs 1.0%, on autos and recreation goods), Canada (0.8% vs 0.4%) and Japan (5.7% vs 5.4%, partly 'naphtha-flation'), and edged down in the Euro area (2.5% vs 2.6%) and UK (1.8% vs 1.9%). Part of global core goods strength reflects consumer electronics price hikes tied to the surge in memory prices.

Core services inflation (3-month annualized) accelerated in most developed markets, partly on firmer airfares: Euro area 3.1% (vs 2.0%), Japan 2.6% (vs 1.5%), US 3.3% (vs 2.5%), UK 4.5% (vs 3.8%). Canada ticked down to 3.5% (vs 4.6%).
Rent inflation (3-month annualized) ticked up in Canada (3.4% vs 2.7%) and the US (2.7% vs 2.3%), was flat in Japan (0.9%), and ticked down in the Euro area (2.4% vs 2.6%) and UK (5.1% vs 5.2%).

Energy inflation (3-month annualized) accelerated across developed markets: UK 52%, Euro area 46%, US 28%, Canada 26%, and Japan -5% (price control measures resumed in September). Food inflation accelerated in the Euro area (2.0% vs -0.1%) and UK (1.7% vs 1.1%) and slowed in Japan, the US and Canada.

Breadth: the share of the headline basket running above 4% (six-month annualized) moderated in Japan (37% vs 48%), the US (23% vs 24%) and the UK (48% vs 49%), and rose in the Euro area (25% vs 23%). Canada is near its historical average at 21%. The share above 8% rose in most markets except Japan.

GS forecasts Q4/Q4 core inflation accelerating to 3.1% in the US (PCE, vs 3.0% now), 3.0% in the UK (vs 2.8%), 2.6% in the Euro area (vs 2.5%), 2.5% in Japan (vs 2.4%) and 2.1% in Canada (vs 1.9%). For 2027 GS expects moderation to 2.2% in the US, 2.7% in the UK, 2.4% in the Euro area, 2.0% in Canada and 0.6% in Japan (largely a food and beverage tax cut starting April 2027).

GS raised 2026 Q4/Q4 headline inflation forecasts over the last month by 0.4pp in Canada and 0.3pp in the US on higher oil prices and wider refined product margins. The Euro area 2026 headline forecast is unchanged and the 2027 headline forecast was cut 0.4pp on faster fuel price normalization. Japan's end-2027 headline and core (ex fresh food) forecasts were raised 0.1pp on energy prices.
GS end-2027 inflation forecasts are generally below consensus (Exhibit 14).

risk_factors: Higher oil prices and wider refined product margins are pushing up headline inflation forecasts (Canada +0.4pp, US +0.3pp for 2026).
Energy inflation accelerated across developed markets, with UK, Euro area and US 3-month annualized rates of 52%, 46% and 28%.
Price hikes for consumer electronics tied to the surge in memory prices are lifting global core goods inflation.
The distribution of three-month inflation rates across core basket items is skewed higher in most developed markets outside Canada.
The share of the basket showing rising year-over-year inflation ticked up across developed markets.

tension_points.bull_case: Trimmed measures (GS trimmed core 2.1% yoy, Dallas Fed 2.3%) run well below traditional core of 3.1%, and GS US economists argue the gap reflects one-off effects of tariffs, the energy shock and AI-related price pressures, so underlying inflation is more benign.
tension_points.bear_case: Traditional core accelerated to 3.1% yoy and 3.9% month-over-month annualized, with core goods, core services and energy all accelerating and GS forecasting core PCE at 3.1% for Q4/Q4 2026.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS expects moderation in 2027 as upstream price pressures fade, to 2.2% for US core; persistent energy and goods strength would undercut the trimmed-mean reading.
